outcome: severe maternal morbidities (e.g., obstetric shock, maternal sepsis, amniotic fluid embolism, renal failure, complications of obstetric interventions, ICU admission)
adverse fetal/infant outcomes (e.g., perinatal death, neonatal mortality, stillbirth)
cohort: The study included all singleton births to women residing in Washington State, US, from 1 January 2003 to 31 December 2013 (n = 828,269).
finding: Maternal age-specific incidence of severe morbidity varied by outcome, with older women (>=40 y) having significantly elevated rates of severe, potentially life-threatening morbidities, and teenage mothers also showing higher rates which mostly attenuated after adjustment for confounders.
